import html # Predefined template for a blog post. The placeholders must be `{title}` and `{body}`. BLOG_FORMAT = """

{title}

{body}
""" def show_blog_post(headline: str, text: str) -> str: """ Return a sanitized and formatted HTML representation of a blog post. Parameters ---------- headline : str The heading/title of the blog post. text : str The main body content of the blog post. Returns ------- str A safe, well‑formed HTML string ready for rendering. Raises ------ TypeError If either argument is not a string. ValueError If the template does not contain the required placeholders. """ # Validate input types if not isinstance(headline, str): raise TypeError(f"headline must be a string, got {type(headline).__name__}") if not isinstance(text, str): raise TypeError(f"text must be a string, got {type(text).__name__}") # Ensure the template has the required placeholders if "{title}" not in BLOG_FORMAT or "{body}" not in BLOG_FORMAT: raise ValueError("BLOG_FORMAT must contain '{title}' and '{body}' placeholders") # Escape user input to prevent XSS safe_headline = html.escape(headline, quote=True) safe_text = html.escape(text, quote=True) # Build the final HTML string formatted_post = BLOG_FORMAT.format(title=safe_headline, body=safe_text) # Basic sanity check: ensure no stray placeholders remain if "{title}" in formatted_post or "{body}" in formatted_post: raise RuntimeError("Unresolved placeholders detected after formatting") return formatted_post
